lede: An economist and management-consulting leader: economic, financial, social and environmental cost-benefit analysis, modelling and feasibility studies, with the research, policy and advocacy insight to carry them into decisions.
summary: Syful Hoque combines economic credentials with long experience leading management consulting work — engaging in-house staff, clients and the global development community in meaningful dialogue. His lead services are economic, financial, social and environmental cost-benefit analysis, modelling and feasibility studies.

He has taken part in more than 100 government and international-donor-funded programmes across the public and private sectors, and has spent 20 years designing, delivering and assessing development, policy and intervention programmes with a focus on South Asia.

His assignments have ranged from agriculture to industrial development, from socio-economic problems to vulnerability and inequality, from infrastructure to technology adoption, from public health to public finance, and from investment to trade policy — research-based and programme-based, sometimes as an economist, sometimes as a researcher, sometimes as a development practitioner.

Across them he has worked with full access to government, the international donor community, research institutions and development banks, local implementers, investors and beneficiaries — and has worked directly with investors and national bodies to leverage resources for investment, preparing business, investment and financing plans and models for national institutes, private companies and large nationwide programmes.

paras: He managed a range of analytical and operational projects and World Bank-commissioned surveys in Bangladesh from scratch — from design and budgeting through research input to implementation, coordination and dissemination.

The role meant balancing competing demands from economists in the Finance, Competitiveness & Innovation (FCI) and Equitable Growth, Finance & Institutions (EFI) Global Practices, alongside ad-hoc research requests from other departments.
